judges_note: All judges recorded here (pathologist, ux-a11y, engineering) were AI agents given role briefs; none is a human professional and no human pathologist judged these concepts. The owner's own review (design/REVIEW-GUIDE.md) is pending as of 2026-11-10. Note and path shortening added 2026-11-10 (audit H1, B7, I-S1).

scores.rationale: At rest this is the screen a 60-case-a-day reader wants: 92 % canvas at 1920, 96 % at 4K, dark neutral chrome, identity fixed top-left, and the whole case is ] ] ] then Shift+Enter then Return to LIS. The corner cluster that fuses navigator, Tier-2 label image, three-slide tray and five summon tabs with their keys printed is the best single idea for muscle memory, and the command echo under the identity line is a genuine teaching device for residents. The safety story is the weakest of the three, though: the mock has no identity-mismatch plate, no session-expired or manifest-failed state and no 'Not complete — do not interpret' string, so the P5/FR-R9 test cannot be passed as presented, and the hand-off dialog lists coverage but never warns about an unviewed slide or offers to open it. Discoverability is thin for a first-week resident (11 px grey summon tabs, right-click radial) and the palette only indexes commands, not slides or sign-out. Mode and product are unmistakable, but the label string still reads '‹laboratory name›' instead of the lab. Keyboard coverage, skip link, live regions and reduced-motion are in place; the strip sign-out button is 22 px and the tablet tabs 26 px, both under target. On iPad the five 44 px bottom targets and the case sheet work well; the embedded Hyperdrive form is the cleanest of the three. The shell is the simplest to build and keep frame-free, although the mock itself re-renders the top bar on every pointer move, which the product must not do.
graft_ideas: Corner cluster: navigator + label image + slide tray (viewed/partial/unviewed) + summon tabs with keys printed, as the only persistent object over the canvas
Command echo under the identity line (visible twin of commandInvoked) to teach the keymap by use
One-drawer-slot rule: one panel open at a time, same place, Esc closes, becomes the bottom sheet on tablet
Radial tool ring at the pointer for right-click / Pencil squeeze / Menu key with the key on each wedge
Keep the small 'Request sign-out ⇧↵' in the status strip so the once-per-case action is visible without a panel (raise it to 24 px)
In-viewport AI legend bottom-right with click-a-class-to-jump and the fixed not-validated marker
Keymap sheet with Default / Left-hand / Right-hand presets and the site's reserved dictation keys struck through

scores.rationale: The Workbench is the most complete and the most explicit: a resident recognises the VS Code / Sectra shape in seconds, nothing is more than one click or two keys away, and the Ctrl+K palette is the only one of the three that finds slides with their viewed state, layout presets, sign-out and Dx. Its best safety ideas are the non-modal sign-out hand-off section that stays open while you keep screening and updates '2 slides not opened' with an Open button, the Dx gate as a six-row checklist that names the failing row and prints the verbatim refusal, and the Clinical-context panel from the LIS that shows prior biopsy and which parts are still scanning, which is exactly what stops a premature sign-out. It is the only mock whose gesture path touches only class, transform and textContent, so P2 discipline is demonstrated rather than promised, and it carries every §6 degraded state including mismatch, expired, manifest 503, context loss and frozen-section TAT. The cost is chrome: 75 % canvas at 1920 and at 4K, 70 % on the laptop with the Inspector floating over tissue, and a dense wall of 12-13 px monospace in the Explorer that a high-volume reader will want gone after day one. Device fit is the weak score: on iPad landscape 42 targets are under 44 px (rail tools 30×28), the embedded form stacks four header rows before the slide, and the two-dock model is the most shell engineering of the three. Focus lands on Return to LIS after Shift+Enter, so a double keystroke can hand back a case with unviewed slides; the warning is visible but not in the way. ARIA is the best of the three (toolbar, keyboard-resizable separators, aria-keyshortcuts, menus) and the canvas-floor governor turns P1 into a measurable rule with the reason stated in the dock header.
graft_ideas: Canvas-floor governor: predict canvas share, degrade least-important chrome first, state what happened and why in the dock header, show the measured share
Non-modal sign-out hand-off section that updates 'n slides not opened' with Open buttons while screening continues
Dx gate as a checklist (build, window, tier, attestation, QA, self-check) with the failing row and the verbatim refusal string
Clinical context from the LIS: prior accession, parts with status such as 'B1 scanning (LIS will update)' and 'C1 not yet scanned'
Palette rows for slides with viewed state, bookmarks, layout presets and every command with its key
In-panel keyboard map with a filter box and the preset selector
Identity verified line under the case card ('launch context matches the manifest before the first tile was drawn')
Frozen-section TAT chip and the Request-consult section that lists exactly what the link carries (Tier 0, expiry, audit)

scores.rationale: Task-flow is the one I would put in front of a PGY-1 and still use myself with Shift+G off: Open → Screen → Examine → Annotate → Sign-out is how a sentinel node is actually read, and every key works at every step so the rail costs the expert nothing but 72 px. Step 1 puts the label image, accession, patient placeholder and three explicit checks (identity match, display attested, launched by whom for what purpose) in front of the reader before high power, which is the strongest wrong-slide defence of the three; the Screen step's coverage bar per slide, 'A2-1 not yet viewed' callout and 'Next unviewed slide ]' are the strongest missed-area defence; and the Sign-out step is a checklist whose dialog warns, offers 'Open A2-1 first', and carries a 'Mark case Reviewed' toggle. It is the only mock that correctly switches the Dx strip to 'Not complete — do not interpret' when tiles fail, and its frozen-consult variant (TAT timer against the CAP 20-minute target, note templates, 'Also page the surgeon', send-preliminary dialog) is the best answer to US-C2 on an iPad. Product and mode are unmistakable with the purpose chip and the lab name in the label string. The accessibility score is held back by five 22 px segmented controls, dimmed layer names at 3.87:1 and badges at 2.67:1, tablet tools 33 px tall and the step drawer and bottom sheet opening by default so the sheet covers 40 % of the slide on iPad portrait (15 central-zone intrusions, the only concept with any). On the laptop the drawer overlays about a fifth of the tissue at step entry, which a sign-out reader will resent until they learn K. Feasibility is fine but two IA modes (flow and plain tabs) plus a per-step tool rail must be maintained together, and the mock's preset keys land on 5.5× mid-animation rather than snapping. Expect 40,000-case attendings to call the Next button a wizard; the mitigation (nothing gated, Shift+G) is real and must stay.
graft_ideas: Five-step reading order (Open, Screen, Examine, Annotate, Sign-out) as the default dock structure with Shift+G collapsing it to plain tabs and N / Shift+N to move
Identity as step 1: label image, accession, patient, specimen, stain, scanner, worklist, plus three check rows for identity match, display attestation and launch user/purpose
Coverage bar per slide, viewed/partial/unviewed by shape, 'Next unviewed slide ]' and the viewed-area trail that never auto-fades
Sign-out checklist with the hand-off dialog's 'Open A2-1 first', 'Keep reviewing' and 'Mark case Reviewed' toggle
Frozen consult: TAT timer against the CAP 20-minute target, preliminary-note templates, 'Also page the surgeon', send-preliminary dialog with evidence attached
AI overlay colours drawn from palette slots the pathologist's own classes never use, outline first, heatmap on demand, lab-validated marker with n
'Not complete — do not interpret' on tile errors in Dx; 'Nav mode · Shift+D enters Dx mode' nudge in the strip on an attested display
Dx-refused banner with a 'Display record I' button; Hyperdrive iframe as a step chip plus tray chips plus 'Open on diagnostic display'

judges.verdict: Concept C (Task-flow) wins on this lens: it makes the top task faster for residents and no slower for experts, and it is the only concept that treats wrong-slide, missed-slide and mode-confusion as first-class steps rather than panels. Build the final sign-out screen on C's five-step structure, but close its two real weaknesses with grafts: adopt B's canvas-floor governor so the step drawer and tablet sheet never open over tissue by default (close on laptop and iPad portrait, open at 1920 and 4K), and adopt A's corner cluster (navigator + label image + tray + summon tabs with printed keys) plus command echo as the at-rest state when the flow is off, so an attending gets A's 92-96 % canvas with C's safety checks still one key away. Take B's non-modal hand-off section, Dx gate checklist and LIS clinical context into C's Sign-out and Open steps, and when any slide is unviewed land focus on 'Open A2-1 first' rather than 'Return to LIS'. Before the critique, fix across all three: 24 px minimum on every segmented control, 44 px tools on iPad landscape, 4.5:1 for layer names even when the layer is off, the lab name in Concept A's label string, and a mismatch, expired and manifest state in whatever ships (A has none). Design notes to carry forward: the 100 µm bar at 20× under the 80-200 px rule (DN-A1/DN-C2), two docks versus region D (DN-B1), the default-open drawer (DN-C4), and the new bindings N/Shift+N/Shift+G/K and U/Shift+U/Shift+P to be filed against the command registry.

scores.rationale: Canvas-maximal is the fastest concept at rest: 92 % canvas at 1080p and 96 % at 4K, no rail or dock, every panel one key away, a radial at the pointer and a command echo that teaches the keymap by use. Product badge, label string, DX indicator and Rendering Complete stay fixed in every state, and the live region speaks at settle ("Rendering Complete. 40 times. A1-1."). Its weaknesses are concentrated in discoverability and safety: the five summon tabs in the navigator cluster are 10 px low-contrast text at 26 px height (unreadable at 4K DPR 1, under the 44 px touch target on the iPad consult surface), and the label image is a thumbnail smaller than B's or C's. The Request sign-out dialog has aria-modal but no focus trap (Tab walks out to the page), hard-codes "Slides viewed 3 of 3" while the tray shows A2-1 unviewed, and has no unviewed-slide guard, so the once-per-case action is the least error-preventing of the three. The keymap and sign-out dialogs are centred over the canvas, against P1's explicit rule that dialogs never cover the centre. Dx availability is not derived from the device class, so the default phone state shows DX. The lab name placeholder is left as "‹laboratory name›". Reduced motion drops to zero animations, pan buttons give the SC 2.5.7 alternative, and the whole shell is trivially frame-cost free, which is why feasibility is highest.
graft_ideas: Command echo under the identity line (visible twin of commandInvoked) as the keymap-teaching device
Summon tabs printed with their keys on the navigator cluster so the navigator doubles as the panel index
Radial tool ring at the pointer / Pencil squeeze, dispatched through the same registry
One drawer slot under the navigator so the eye learns one place; sheets on portrait
Canvas-share targets of 92 % / 96 % as the bar the final layout should approach at rest
Measure-tool status line bottom-left ("click two points · Space pan · Esc cancel")

scores.rationale: Workbench buys learnability and completeness: Explorer (identity, hanging-protocol tray with coverage, layers with provenance) and Inspector (LIS clinical context and prior, measure, compare, consult, hand-off, keymap) are always one click away, and a canvas-floor governor degrades chrome mechanically and says why ("Narrowed to the slide strip so the canvas stays ≥ 70 %"). It is the only concept whose dialogs obey P1: the sign-out hand-off is a non-modal Inspector section that updates live and warns "2 slides not opened" with an Open A1-2 button, the Dx gate is a per-gate checklist popover anchored top-right with the failing row bold and the Enter button disabled, and the palette anchors top-left. It is also the only concept that derives Dx availability from the device class at runtime, so the phone and tablet correctly show NAV, Pitch unknown and the Tier 2 string. Semantics are the richest (aria-expanded accordions, role=separator resizers with arrow keys, toolbar roles, a live region that reports magnification, position and unviewed count), the canvas is focused on load, and reduced motion zeroes all 37 transitions. Costs: 75 % canvas at rest on the diagnostic display and 70 % on the laptop, two docks that split attention, 9-10 px key hints and a 9 px "label · Tier 2" tag, Outline/Heatmap and Lock/Affine/None at 18-20 px, and at 1366 landscape (iPad with Pencil) the desktop rail stays at 30×28 px. Esc from the hand-off panel drops focus onto the page instead of the canvas, and Esc inside the keymap filter never closes the floating keymap despite the rationale's claim. Two resizable docks plus a floating mode are more MVP shell work than A or C.
graft_ideas: Canvas-floor governor: predicted canvas share drives which chrome degrades first, with the reason stated in the dock header and the share measurable
Dx gate as a checklist popover (build, window, tier, attestation, QA, self-check) with the exact refusal string and a disabled Enter button
Sign-out hand-off as a non-modal panel that keeps updating while reviewing, with the unviewed-slide warning and Open-next shortcut
Runtime device-class gating (pointer: coarse, width, surface) that forces NAV, ~mag and Pitch unknown on tablets/phones/iframes
Keyboard map generated from the command registry with filter, presets and reserved Dragon/Hyperdrive keys greyed
Clinical context from the LIS (specimen parts, prior accession, scanning status) in the dock
Explorer narrowed to an identity-plus-slides strip as the minimum identity surface that never disappears
Rich polite live region: magnification, µm/px, centre position, slide opened and unviewed count

scores.rationale: Task-flow organises the shell around how a case is actually read (Open → Screen → Examine → Annotate → Sign-out) and gives each step one panel, one primary action and only that step's tools, which produces the clearest hierarchy of the three: identity is step 1 with a large label image and three verification lines, screening carries a coverage contract with "Next unviewed slide ]", the layer rows distinguish research (fixed FR-R11 marker) from lab-validated (n = 62) overlays, and sign-out is a checklist that previews exactly what returns to the LIS, warns about A2-1, offers Open A2-1 first and a Mark Reviewed toggle. Guided-off turns the same panels into plain tabs, so the expert loses nothing, and the frozen-consult variant (flow bar, TAT timer against the CAP 20-minute target, note templates, 44 px pen tool bar with polygon/freehand/measure) is the best tablet story. Keyboard behaviour is the cleanest measured: the sign-out dialog traps focus, Esc returns to the canvas, the palette filters to "Measure length", and the live region announces the fit-to-slide on slide change. Failures to fix: the keymap, palette and sign-out dialogs are centred over the canvas (P1 forbids dialogs in the centre), focus order puts the step rail before the canvas, and the keymap opens with focus on Close. Dock controls (presets, lock/affine/none, Outline/Heatmap) are 22-28 px and stay that size under a coarse pointer, phone step chips are 28×30 px and the phone sheet reaches 56 % of the viewport. State honesty slips in three places: the default phone state shows DX, the Dx-refused state keeps "pitch EDID" and the QA chip, and the 1366 offline consult strip clips its notice and duplicates the pack chip. Canvas share is 73 % at 1080p (84 % at 4K); the drawer opens by default on step entry at laptop width, which the owner should test for friction.
graft_ideas: Identity-first step: label image, accession, patient, specimen, launch user/purpose and three verification lines before the first high-power view
Screening panel with per-slide coverage, "A2-1 not yet viewed" and a Next-unviewed-slide command
Sign-out checklist that previews the evidence returning to the LIS and blocks nothing but warns, with Open-first and Mark-Reviewed controls
Frozen-section consult flow: TAT timer vs CAP 20 min, preliminary-note templates, Request consult, Send to OR
Contextual tool rail per step with the full rail one toggle away (guided flow off)
Flow bar at the top and 44 px pen tool bar at the bottom on tablet portrait
Research vs lab-validated layer markers side by side, overlays off by default in Dx

judges.verdict: Winner under the UX and accessibility lens: clinical-signout-c (Task-flow), total 49/60 versus 44 for A and 44 for B. C has the strongest hierarchy, the safest sign-out and screening (unviewed-slide guard, evidence preview, identity-first step), the only pen-first tablet tool bar, and the cleanest keyboard behaviour (true focus trap, Esc restores focus, settle-based announcements). Conditions for the final design: (1) move the keymap, palette and sign-out off the canvas centre, following B's dock-anchored panels and popovers (P1 explicitly forbids centred dialogs); (2) adopt B's runtime device-class gating so phones, tablets and iframes always show NAV, ~mag and Pitch unknown, and make the Dx-refused state drop the QA chip and EDID pitch line; (3) raise all dock controls to 24 px on desktop and 44 px under pointer: coarse, cap the phone sheet at 40 %, and put the canvas before the rail in tab order; (4) fix the status-strip overflow by allowing one notice plus chips, never two notices; (5) borrow A's canvas-share discipline (command echo, summon tabs on the navigator, radial at the pointer) so the Examine step can collapse toward A's 92 % canvas on the diagnostic display, and B's canvas-floor governor to make that collapse mechanical and explained. Concept A should not win: its modal has no focus trap, its sign-out dialog misreports slide coverage with no unviewed guard, and its 10 px cluster tabs fail legibility at 4K and target size on touch. Concept B is the runner-up and the source of the most reusable mechanisms (governor, Dx gate checklist, non-modal hand-off, registry-generated keymap).

scores.rationale: Canvas-maximal is the cheapest shell of the three: one-column grid, a navigator cluster composed from existing tray/tab/navigator classes, one drawer slot and 40 page-level classes (B has 88, C 59); measured canvas share is 92.6 % at 1920x1080 and 96.3 % at 4K, far above P1. Every live element maps to a named contract (launch context, state document, layer API, tileSettled/renderingcomplete, command bus) and the single command registry drives keys, palette, radial, bottom bar and the keymap, which is exactly how a Lit shell over the command bus should be built; the headless probe confirmed ?, Ctrl+K, ], Shift+Enter and presets work and Alt/F-keys are ignored. The engineering debits: the radial is declared a transient GPU layer (custom engine work: glyph-atlas icons plus hit testing) or else it is DOM over the canvas; the command echo makes the top-left HUD box change height during gestures (the only chrome geometry change the probe found in any concept, hud#hudTL grew from 1 to 2 lines), so it must become a fixed-height slot; the mock never sets .is-gesturing and rebuilds the drawer/badge/tool states on every wheel notch (182 chrome mutations, 66 childList, for one drag plus six notches), a mock artefact but also a sign that HUD and chrome updates are not separated; keys stay bound in the embedded iframe variant despite the rationale's rule-5 claim; typed zoom is a toast stub. Workflow-wise it is fast for a keyboard-first expert but weak for AI-assisted screening (layers live behind Shift+H in a single slot shared with marks and compare), the sign-out dialog carries no unviewed-slide warning (B and C both do), and discoverability rests on 10 px summon-tab labels and a right-click. Targets are mostly fine (one 22 px strip button) and reduced motion is honoured, but tablet touch targets in the cluster (30 px thumbnails, 26 px tabs) fall below the 44 px touch rule even though the bottom bar is 44 px.
graft_ideas: One command registry object that renders the keymap sheet, the palette, the rail/bottom bar and the key handler, with reserved dictation keys struck through everywhere
Command echo under the identity line as the visible twin of the proposed commandInvoked event (implemented as a fixed-height HUD slot so it never re-lays out)
Summon-tab key hints printed on the navigator cluster so the keymap is taught in place
Hanging-protocol line in the case panel (opened fit-to-slide, H&E before IHC) and the snapshot 'Label image included' tier chip
Radial tool at the pointer as a later, DOM-only, static-time option (never during a gesture)

scores.rationale: Workbench is the best-engineered mock (syncCam updates HUD text only during a drag, .is-gesturing is set on pointerdown, list rebuilds happen in afterGesture at pointerup: 67 chrome mutations all at gesture end and zero chrome geometry change) and it is the only concept that binds no keys inside the EHR iframe, which is principles §4.5 rule 5 by construction. It is also by far the most custom shell for an MVP: two docks with accordion sections that can be hidden, moved between docks and reordered, keyboard-resizable splitters, a canvas-floor governor that reads computed styles and predicts share, five layout presets remembered per surface and user, an activity bar, three collapsed forms (slide strip, identity ribbon, horizontal slide row), a floating inspector, dock-anchored popovers, and an analytics panel with coverage bars and a dwell histogram; 88 page-level classes against 40 and 59. Two panels imply contracts the plan does not have: 'Clinical context from LIS' (narrative history, prior accessions, specimen parts) and the frozen TAT chip need a read API from the integration service that is outside the launch-context contract of plan 04 §8 / plan 12 §1.1 and carries PHI, so they are a Design note, not a graft. Smaller debits: typed zoom uses window.prompt(), which sandboxed Hyperdrive iframes block; dragging a splitter re-lays out the grid and therefore resizes the engine surface every frame; segmented items are 18 to 20 px tall and the splitters 7 px wide (keyboard alternatives exist). The canvas share is 75 % at 1920 and 70.6 % at 1440 with the inspector floating over tissue, so the workbench promise is only fully realised at 4K; the top bar is crowded enough that container queries have to drop the worklist chip, slide and meta below 1600 px. Accessibility is strong: real buttons for accordions, role=separator with arrow keys, toolbar and listbox roles, polite/assertive regions, two-click measure. The Dx gate as a six-row checklist, the live non-modal sign-out section that updates its '2 slides not opened' warning while screening, and the 'AI-flagged regions viewed at >= 10x' line are ideas worth keeping regardless of the winner.
graft_ideas: Dx gate rendered as a checklist (build, window, tier, attestation, QA, self-check) with the first failure's exact refusal string, reused by the strip and live region
Sign-out hand-off as a live-updating non-modal section with the unviewed-slide warning and an 'Open A1-2' action, not only a modal
The 70 % canvas floor as an explicit per-surface layout table (static, decided at breakpoint) rather than a runtime measurer; keep the dock header note that says what collapsed and why
No keys bound inside the EHR iframe; Ctrl+K there shows the companion-window notice
'AI-flagged regions viewed at >= 10x' via geometry pointInPolygon x viewChanged, surfaced in the sign-out evidence
Collapsed Explorer as a slide strip (label thumbnail, accession, slide thumbnails) so identity and tray never disappear
Layer visibility set to the Dx default (AI off, label image not collapsible) on Dx entry, with the 'pinned · Dx' marker

scores.rationale: Task-flow is the most buildable concept that still shows the whole must-show list: one standard rail/dock frame from base.css, one dock whose five step panels are static markup toggled by a class, per-step tool visibility done with the hidden attribute, the step list rendered from one array into rail, flow bar and dialog, dialogs cloned from templates, and every control mapped to a named contract (flow.goto on the command bus is shell-only state). It implements .is-gesturing on drag, wheel and flyTo, forces transition:none on the canvas, keeps chrome geometry fixed during gestures (probe: zero chrome geometry change at all five viewports), and its measured canvas share is 73.7 % at 1920, 84.2 % at 4K, 86.6 % at 1440 (drawer closed) and 85.7 % on the tablet. The one performance fault is that paintView writes dock state every frame (216 attribute writes in a short drag plus six notches: preset aria-pressed, presetCount text, canvas aria-label, strip indicator class); in the product those writes move to settle, a small fix, but the design should state that only HUD text updates per frame. The TAT timer and 'received 09:41' need LIS timestamps that are not in the launch-context contract, and the preliminary note write-back is Clinical-IH-only FR-I6 (v1), both correctly labelled; keys remain bound inside the iframe variant, which is acceptable for the embedded compact viewer (Design note D7) but not for the controller iframe. Workflow fit is the strongest: identity before pixels as step 1, a coverage contract in the Screen step, AI overlays off by default in Dx with vendor/status/marker rows, a sign-out checklist that warns about A2-1 and offers to open it first, and a frozen consult that is the same flow with two steps renamed; nothing is gated and Shift+G collapses the flow to plain tabs for experts. Device fit is the best of the three: 84 px rail at 4K, flow bar plus 44 px bottom bar plus a <= 40 % sheet on tablet portrait, pen draws while a finger pans with pinch handled, and the phone collapses the flow bar to numbers with the current label. Clarity and accessibility are good (aria-current=step, shape not colour for attention, focus trap in dialogs, live regions, reduced motion disables flyTo), with five 22 px segmented buttons and 10 px uppercase rail labels as the main target/legibility debits. Its ideas are less novel than A's or B's, which is partly why it is cheaper.
graft_ideas: Five-step reading order (Open, Screen, Examine, Annotate, Sign-out) as the default dock tab order even without the step header, so power users get plain tabs with the same contents
Identity card as the first panel: label image, launch user/role/purpose, identity-check line and display attestation line
Screen step coverage contract: per-slide coverage bars, 'A2-1 not yet viewed' status line and Next-unviewed-slide action; viewed state returned at sign-out
Sign-out checklist listing exactly what returns to the LIS (status, viewed state, SR/ANN evidence, AI accept/reject, render mode and display record, audit) mirrored in the hand-off dialog
AI overlay classes drawn in palette slots the pathologist's own classes never use (teal/amber dashed), with the lab-validated marker beside the FR-R11 marker
Embedded iframe collapse to a step chip plus tray chips plus 'Open on diagnostic display'
Frozen consult as the same flow with Note/Send steps and templates; Dx refused with the Tier-2 string

judges.verdict: Recommend Concept C (Task-flow) as the base for the final clinical sign-out screen, with grafts from A and B. From the front-end/engine lens C is the design that covers the entire must-show list on one standard rail/dock frame with the least custom component work that still has a credible tablet/pen story: a single dock, static step panels, per-step tool visibility by attribute, templated dialogs, .is-gesturing implemented on drag/wheel/flyTo, and no chrome geometry change during gestures at any of the five viewports (headless probe). Its one performance defect (paintView writing dock button state every frame, 216 attribute writes per short gesture) is a one-afternoon fix: only HUD text may update per frame, everything else at settle. Concept A is the cheapest shell (40 custom classes, 92.6 % canvas at 1920) and its single command registry, command echo and summon-tab key hints should be carried over, but it depends on an engine-drawn radial for tool access, grows a HUD box during gestures, rebuilds drawers per wheel notch, binds keys inside the iframe, and leaves AI-assisted screening and the unviewed-slide hazard weak. Concept B is the best-structured mock (HUD-only updates during drag, no keys in the iframe) and contributes the Dx-gate checklist, the live non-modal hand-off section and the AI-flagged-regions-viewed line, but as an MVP shell it is the most expensive by a wide margin (two docks, movable sections, resizers that resize the engine surface per frame, a runtime governor, five persisted presets, analytics) and two of its panels assume a clinical-context/timestamp read API that the launch-context contract does not provide; its 70 to 75 % canvas on 1440/1920 displays is also the weakest of the three. Design notes for the final: replace C's per-frame dock writes with settle-time updates, adopt B's no-keys-in-iframe rule for the controller iframe, treat the TAT/clinical-context data as a new integration-service contract to be filed with an FR- id, and keep A's radial as a static-time, DOM-only, post-MVP option.

synthesis.summary: Final clinical sign-out viewer (Stoipath Clinical-IH / Dx) written to wsi-viewer/design/screens/final/clinical-signout.html (240 KB, self-contained, links ../../design-system/tokens.css and base.css by relative path, no network, 88 data-live markers, 21 data-synthetic markers). Structure is Concept C's five-step flow (Open → Screen → Examine → Annotate → Sign-out: 72 px step rail with per-step tools, one dock panel per step, N/Shift+N, Shift+G to plain tabs, K for the panel; flow bar + 44 px bottom bar + ≤40 % sheet on touch; Hyperdrive iframe as step chip + tray chips + hand-off). Grafts from B: static per-surface layout policy (panel open at ≥1600 px, closed on laptop/iPad with the reason printed in the dock header and the measured share in the review header), seven-row Dx gate checklist with the verbatim refusal string and a disabled Enter, the Sign-out step as a live non-modal hand-off list that updates while screening (confirm dialog focuses "Open A2-1 first" when a slide is unviewed, "Return to LIS" otherwise), runtime device-class gating (coarse pointer / <1080 px / iframe → NAV, ~20×, Pitch unknown, QA chip dropped), clinical context from the LIS and the frozen TAT timer (marked as a proposed read contract), palette rows for slides with viewed state/bookmarks/steps/layouts, registry-generated keymap with filter and presets, no keys bound inside the iframe (Ctrl+K shows the companion-window notice). Grafts from A: the navigator becomes the corner cluster (viewport + trail, label image, three slide thumbnails with viewed state, five summon tabs with printed keys on a 3+2 grid) whenever the panel is closed, a fixed-height command-echo HUD slot, the in-viewport AI legend with the FR-R11 marker, the measure-tool status line, and the 24 px strip sign-out button. All dialogs are anchored over the dock column (palette over the rail column) with widths chosen per breakpoint so they never cross the central 50 % zone; the dialog layer is non-blocking and click-outside closes. Twelve degraded states are switchable (cold 4G, offline pack, slow translator, tile errors, Dx refused, QA overdue, Dx dropped, identity mismatch, session expired, manifest 503, GPU context loss) using the principles §5 microcopy verbatim; one strip notice at a time. A collapsed "Design decisions" section lists what was taken from which concept and why, the judge disagreements and their resolution, fixes applied across all three concepts, the engine-contract map, canvas shares per surface, design notes DN-F1 to DN-F9 and known mock weaknesses. Screenshots at the six required viewports plus twelve state shots are in wsi-viewer/design/screens/final/shots/; every screenshot was inspected and the problems found were fixed before finishing.
notes: Measured canvas share at rest (headless Chromium, app frame excluding review chrome): 4K 84.0 % (panel open), 1920 73.2 % (panel open; 86 % with the cluster), 1440 85.8 % (panel closed by policy), 1366x1024 touch 86.2 %, 1024x1366 touch 84.8 %, 390x844 81.8 %; embedded iframe 91.8 %. Defaults on touch surfaces select the frozen-consult variant (Consultation · preliminary only), NAV, ~20× and Pitch unknown.

Headless audit at all 18 shots: no console or page errors, no horizontal overflow, no visible target under 24 px (44 px under pointer: coarse), no UI in the central 50 % x 50 % zone except the user-opened dock sheet on portrait tablet/phone (documented as DN-F5). Gesture probe (drag + six wheel notches at 1920): zero chrome geometry change, zero dock/top-bar/navigator mutations; the only chrome writes are the strip indicator flipping to Rendering…/Sharpening (class + label) at gesture start; tray, checklist, preset state and aria labels update at settle only. A gesture now cancels any pending settle timer.

Behaviour verified by probe: N/Shift+N move steps without reopening the laptop drawer; Shift+G yields plain tabs with all 17 tools; K closes the panel and the navigator grows into the 320 px cluster; Shift+Enter opens the anchored sign-out dialog with focus on 'Open A2-1 first' (focus trapped; Esc returns focus to the canvas); after all slides are viewed the warning disappears and focus lands on 'Return to LIS'; Shift+D leaves Dx, a second Shift+D opens the 7-row gate (Enter disabled when a row fails: QA overdue, no attestation, tablet, iframe, RUO, mismatch); Ctrl+K palette finds 'Open slide A2-1 · not viewed'; ? opens the keymap on its filter; right-click opens the context menu at the pointer; in the iframe variant N, Shift+Enter and Ctrl+K do nothing except the companion-window notice; resizing 1920→1440 closes the panel by policy and 1440→1920 reopens it; tile errors in Dx switch the strip to 'Not complete — do not interpret' after 2 s with an assertive announcement.

Judge disagreements decided: laptop drawer closed by default (static policy table replaces C's DN-C4 and B's runtime governor); all dialogs anchored, none centred (ux-a11y condition 1); one dock, not B's two (DN-B1); the step rail stays but nothing is gated (pathologist's wizard concern); B's clinical context and TAT kept but labelled as a proposed integration-service contract (engineering).

Design notes to file (listed in the page): DN-F1 new bindings N, Shift+N, Shift+G, K (and Shift+Q from map B) against the command registry; DN-F2 scale bar 100 µm at 20× under the 80–200 px rule (the brief's '200 µm at 20×' cannot hold at DPR 1); DN-F3 LIS clinical context and frozen timestamps need an FR- id (PHI, outside the launch-context contract); DN-F4 layout policy table makes principles §7 explicit; DN-F5 sheets on touch cover the lower central zone while open; DN-F6 A's radial deferred, plan §4.1 context menu shipped; DN-F7 label-image tier on an in-lab iPad; DN-F8 preset ladder per D8; DN-F9 RUO product shows the launch-refused plate.

Mock limitations (also in the page): synthetic SVG tissue; sharpening/Dx verifier simulated by timers; rotation, curtain, snapshot, B/C/γ panel are toast stubs; only lock sync honoured; coverage not computed from true viewport union; measurement labels scale with zoom; tested in headless Chromium only (mouse, keyboard, touch taps), no Apple Pencil hover or pressure. Screenshot and probe scripts live in the session scratchpad (<scratch>/final/shoot.js and probe.js), not in the repo. No git commands were run.

scores.rationale: As the 4K reader this is the concept I would reach for first: 92 % canvas at 1920 and 96 % at 3840 (measured), two labelled edge handles, a radial tool wheel under the pointer with its keys printed, and one fixed reading surface (the bottom-centre step card) that doubles as the caption track and the polite live region, so I never hunt for the question. The keyboard path works end to end (Shift+Enter opens six candidates with Fly there, Enter commits, Shift+R reveals, and the live region speaks 'Revealed. Your mark overlapped the lesion by 62 percent'); the palette's 'Not in this build' group that answers 'dx' with 'Dx mode is not part of Stoipath Learn' is the clearest mode statement of the three. For teaching, though, the course hierarchy is hidden behind Shift+K, the stepper is a 4 px rail of ticks a student will not notice and a thumb cannot hit (28 px tall under a coarse pointer), and the design's own Shift+R overload (reveal while committed, rotate otherwise, DN-A2) is exactly the kind of muscle-memory trap a resident who alternates between the Learn and clinical builds will fall into. Measured misses: the step card intrudes into the central 50 % zone at 1440×900 and on the phone, where the sheet takes 41 % of the viewport; the confidence buttons are 18 px tall (SC 2.5.8) and the card toolbar is 40 px on touch; the candidates dialog lands focus on the Close button rather than the list; and after a fly-to the mock exposes a dark-grey uncovered strip beside tissue (a mock artefact, but it is the one 'blank canvas' a pathologist will see in the review). Feasibility is good because there is so little chrome and panels only change between gestures, but the Pencil-squeeze radial depends on Pencil Pro hardware. Phone resident variant (differential chips, timer, offline chip in the HUD, sharpness dot) is well judged. Director analytics drawn as a layer over the actual slide is the view I would use in a resident meeting.
graft_ideas: Step card as a caption track at bottom-centre: tour text, item stem, feedback and reveal all appear in the same fixed place and are the same string the live region speaks
Edge handles that stay visible and print their key (Module ⇧K, Step K) so folded chrome is never a mystery
Radial tool wheel at the pointer (right-click / long-press / Pencil) with each tool's key printed, as the 4K expert mode where the rail is folded
Command palette group 'Not in this build' that answers a Dx/sign-out query with the refusal microcopy
Director analytics as overlay layers on the real slide (dwell as luminance, expert path, cohort median path) with an aggregate-only guard
Offline-pack and sharpness state shown in the HUD on the phone where the strip has no room
'Choose a region instead' button on the item card itself, not only behind a shortcut

scores.rationale: The Workbench is the safest engineering bet and the one whose grammar transfers directly from the clinical and research builds: rail, left panel, dock, status strip, Ctrl+K palette with everything (40 entries) and a keymap that greys out the site's reserved dictation keys. Its keyboard path is the smoothest of the three (Enter inside the candidates dialog commits, Shift+R reveals, and the assertive region announces 'Revealed ... Posted to gradebook'), the resizers are keyboard-operable separators, and the laptop context bar that keeps the stem, gate and Commit in one neutral 36 px line is a genuinely good idea. As an educator I would refuse the default learner dock as shown: while item 4 'Mark the metastatic focus' is live, the Review queue sits directly under it listing 'Tingible-body macrophages vs metastasis', 'ITC vs micrometastasis threshold' and 'Sinus histiocytosis pattern', which is a differential handed to the student mid-assessment; spaced-retrieval content must never share a screen with a graded item. Clarity suffers from density: the dock body runs at 12 px, the canvas is 74 % at 1920 (passing, but the concept's own look needs ≥2560 px to appear), and the schematic tissue reads as a diagram at every magnification, with the expert path drawn as black lines across the 20× field. Measured target misses: Captions/Transcript/Fly-to chips at 22 px, confidence at 18 px, and on an iPad the sheet's Skip, Text alternative and expand/collapse buttons stay 24 px. The phone is the weakest surface of all nine screens I compared: at 0.2× the slide is a small thumbnail in a dark field that reads as a blank canvas, and the navigator is hidden. Feasibility is high (fixed grid tracks, panels as details, resize deferred while gesturing). The publish lint that blocks publishing a region item without candidates and a rubric, and the role-swapped Author/Director panel sets, are worth keeping.
graft_ideas: Laptop context bar: when the dock folds, the item stem, zoom gate, text-alternative key and Commit survive as one neutral line outside the central zone
Enter inside the candidates dialog commits the chosen candidate directly; reveal announces score and gradebook status in the assertive live region in one sentence
Publish lint in the author studio: keyboard alternative present, text rubric present, no red–green-only meaning, licence and determination logged, captions required before publish
Palette groups for Fly-to candidates, layout presets and settings so every learner action is reachable by search with its key shown
Keymap sheet that greys out keys reserved at the site (dictation push-to-talk) and names the active preset
IoU distribution histogram and item p/discrimination table in the director view, computed only for n ≥ 30
Keyboard-resizable panels (role=separator with arrow keys)

scores.rationale: This is how I actually teach a sentinel node: survey at low power, examine the sinus, decide, compare with the attending. The step rail (Open → Screen → Examine → Decide → Complete) makes that sequence the shell, discloses only the tools each phase needs (no polygon tool during the survey, a real mode-error reducer), and ends every card in one 56 px primary action a thumb or Pencil can hit without looking. The pedagogy details are the best in the set: 'Low-power coverage 64 %' during Screen (scanning rate, not zoom rate, predicts accuracy), an explicit gate rule ('commit now for half credit, or press 5 to jump to 20×'), a stale-tile reveal guard that honours plan 01's 'a region-marking item with a soft tile is an unfair item', a card header that says GRADED · CANVAS or Practice · not graded, confidence that 'feeds your review queue, not your grade', the review queue kept to the Complete phase rather than beside a live item, and 'Fly to what you missed' in the compare step, which is the one feature I would demand in any final design. The resident unknown (ranked differential with move up/down buttons, 'Diagnosis recorded 06:12 into the case', reveal as a layer-ACL gate) and the record-a-tour studio (view + ink + voice, a pause over 2 s cuts a step) are both credible, and the Dx-refused variant with DX badge, NAV indicator, 'Consultation · preliminary only' chip, label image and the hand-off-to-attested-display dialog proves the shell does not fork per build. The keyboard path completes (Shift+Enter → C → Enter → Enter → Shift+R → 'Revealed · candidate C · 1/1, modality: keyboard') and announce() is wired to commit, reveal, dialog open, step change and layer toggles. The dents are measurable: the canvas is 70.3 % at 1920 standalone (no P1 margin) because the rail is 84 px and the dock 360; the expanded bottom sheet intrudes into the central zone by the concept's own admission; on an iPad the navigator pan buttons stay 24×24 and the phase buttons are 30–38 px wide, which is odd for a tablet-first concept; and the dotted-pattern tissue mock reads as wallpaper at 20×, the least convincing of the three. Feasibility is a notch lower than A and B because of per-audience step lists, per-phase tool filtering and the peek/expand sheet, but nothing here needs more than the state document, layer ACLs, geometry services and the command bus already in the contracts, and the code already zeroes chrome transitions while gesturing and uses contain: layout paint style.
graft_ideas: Phase rail Open → Screen → Examine → Decide → Complete with tools disclosed per phase and an 'All tools' switch for experts
One primary action per step (56 px CTA at the card foot) with Previous / Skip to the question / All keys as a secondary row
Card header states graded vs practice vs CME post-test vs ungraded unknown, and the LMS/gradebook destination
Low-power coverage % during the survey step and 'did you view the lower border' feedback; 'Fly to what you missed' in the compare step
Explicit zoom-gate economics: half credit below 20× with 'press 5 to jump to 20×', highest magnification reached over the focus reported live
Reveal refused while a tile under the mark is stale (honest pixels inside the item engine)
Ranked differential with move up/down buttons as the SC 2.5.7 alternative to drag; 'Diagnosis recorded mm:ss into the case'
Record-a-tour with VIEW/INK/MIC chips, pause-cuts-a-step, and caption requirement before publish
'Marked by keyboard · C' chip and director KPI 'completed by keyboard path / text answer · scores identical by modality'
Hand-off-for-sign-out dialog on a non-attested device in the clinical variant, showing the shell scales without forking

judges.verdict: Concept C (Task-flow) wins for the pathologist-educator role (an AI agent judge, not a human pathologist): it is the only one whose shell is the teaching method itself (survey → examine → decide → compare), it keeps assessment hygiene (no review-queue hints beside a live item, graded/practice stated on the card, stale-tile reveal guard, explicit half-credit gate), it is the strongest on the iPad with a Pencil and on the phone, and its keyboard path, announcements and Dx-refusal handling are correct. Its fixes are concrete: bring the navigator pan buttons and phase buttons to 44 px under a coarse pointer, buy back canvas at 1920 (64 px rail with labels on hover, or a 320 px dock) so P1 has margin, replace the expanding bottom sheet with a side sheet in landscape, and give the tissue mock a convincing 20× field before the owner reviews it. Graft from A the 4K expert mode (fold the rail and dock into labelled edge handles, keep the caption-track step card at bottom-centre, add the radial at the pointer and the palette's 'Not in this build' answer for Dx), and from B the laptop context bar, Enter-commits-from-the-candidates-dialog with the assertive one-sentence reveal announcement, the publish lint, and the keyboard-resizable panels. Cross-concept design note for the principles owner: all three bind Shift+R to reveal while map A binds it to rotate anticlockwise; resolve it once (reveal should take a key that no clinical action uses) before any final screen is built.

scores.rationale: The canvas-maximal angle serves the resident and the 4K reader superbly (96 % canvas measured at 3840x2160, 93 % at 1920) and the single bottom-centre step card is a sound idea: tour text, stem, feedback and reveal always appear in one place and the card is the literal twin of the polite live region (the N key announces 'Step 5 of 9. Confirm with IHC.' correctly). For the Learn persona, though, the top task gets slower before it gets faster: the module list, review queue and settings sit behind two 28 px edge handles and a 4 px stepper rail, tools are behind right-click/long-press, and the rationale itself concedes a formative test is needed. The card floats over tissue and, at 1440x900, overlaps the central 50 % zone (11.6k px² measured) despite the claim that it never does; on the phone the sheet is 44 % of the viewport at rest and the navigator is still shown. Accessibility is the weakest of the three in the runtime checks: the candidates dialog does not trap focus (Tab walks out of an aria-modal dialog), initial focus lands on Close, candidates are not an arrow-key radiogroup, the stepper ticks' only focus indicator is a 4 px bar turning the same grey as the current step (weak 2.4.7), the confidence segments are 18 px tall (2.5.8), and on coarse pointers 22 of 31 targets are under 44 px including the primary Commit button at 24 px and the tour controls at 40 px. There are no headings in the DOM, so screen-reader users cannot jump to the item. Product and mode are unmistakable on desktop, but the full Learn string disappears at 1024 wide where the IA keeps it. Reduced motion is handled well (transitions zeroed, a HUD chip says 'fly-to jumps'), degraded states live honestly in the strip, and the keymap, palette and launch-refusal plate are complete. A strong expert viewer; not yet a safe first-run learner shell.
graft_ideas: Radial tool menu at the pointer with the key printed on each item, as the pen/touch transient layer (Pencil squeeze, long-press)
HUD chip 'Reduced motion · fly-to jumps' so learners see why a fly-to became a cut
Card text and polite live region share one string (captions are the SR text)
'Score pending · posts to the gradebook on reveal' line before S27, then 'Posting…' in the strip
Launch-refusal plate for a wrong-product launch that keeps the LEARN badge above it
Thin progress rail along the canvas top edge with per-step tooltips (rebuild with 24 px targets and a real focus ring)
Keymap sheet lists 'Never bound: F1–F12, Alt' explicitly and names the preset

scores.rationale: The Workbench is the most conventional and the best-engineered shell: panels are grid tracks beside the canvas rather than DOM over it, resizing is deferred while gesturing, the dock is a keyboard-resizable role=separator, and the measured canvas share holds P1 at every width (74 % at 1920, 87 % at 1440, 88 % tablet, 85 % phone). Its laptop story is the strongest of the three: when the dock folds, a one-line context bar keeps the stem, the zoom gate, the ⇧↵ text alternative and Commit visible, and the zoom-gate chip sits next to the magnification readout where the eye already is. The keyboard model passed every runtime check: visible focus on all 40 tab stops, the candidates dialog traps focus, opens on the current candidate, moves and checks with arrow keys, Escape returns focus to the canvas, and the Ctrl+K palette surfaces steps, candidates, layout presets and settings with their keys, which is the discoverability layer the IA asks for. Hierarchy is the cost: the item card is third in a dock stack under the tour player, Commit is pinned to the dock foot (about 900 px below the stem at 4K), and the author page is dense. State communication is good but incomplete for screen readers: pressing N announces 'Flew to 40×' and not the new step title. Target sizes slip in the small print: chips 22 px and confidence segments 18 px tall on desktop, and on tablet the 'Text alternative' and 'Skip' buttons are 24 px tall while the expand/collapse icons are 24 px squares; the expanded phone sheet reaches 66 %. The module title truncates at 1440 and is dropped below 1024 (only 'PATH 611 · 4/9' remains), which weakens P4 on tablets. Degraded states use the §5 strings verbatim with a Retry chip, captions default on with a transcript, and the CVD and reduced-motion toggles are in both Settings and the palette. A safe, learnable choice whose main risk is that the learner's question competes with five other panels for attention.
graft_ideas: Context bar in the banner slot when the dock folds on laptops: stem · zoom gate · ⇧↵ · Commit in one neutral line
Zoom-gate chip anchored beside the magnification readout ('now 5× · need ≥ 20× [5]')
Command palette rows for every candidate region, step, layer and layout preset with their keys
Keyboard-resizable dock via role=separator with arrow keys; pin as a logged user choice
Candidates dialog pattern: focus opens on the current candidate, arrow keys move and check, Fly there per row
Sheet 'peek' state with grabber plus an Expand button (drag alternative) at about 230 px
'Expert's view' collapsible with thumbnail, legend and your-vs-expert stats, unlocked at reveal
Author studio button 'Sign-out annotations → teaching layers' and the publish lint tagging candidates A–F as required

scores.rationale: Task-flow makes the learner's top task both faster and safer: every step has exactly one primary action at a fixed place (a 52–56 px CTA that ↵ also runs), the card states the item's status in two chips ('Awaiting your answer', 'Zoom gate 20× met'), the zoom gate is reported honestly as the highest magnification reached over the focus, reveal is a gate on itemAnswered that refuses while a tile under the mark is stale, and confidence is labelled 'feeds your review queue, not your grade' with a calibration line at reveal. 'Mark without a pointer' is a visible secondary button in the card and a tool in the rail, not a hint in small print, and the author cannot publish a region item without an alternative, which is NFR-A5 enforced rather than recommended. It is the only concept with zero sub-24 px targets on desktop; every tab stop shows a ring; the candidates dialog has an h2, tabs for 'Answer in text', a focus-trapped arrow-key radiogroup opening on the current candidate, and Escape returns focus to the canvas; on a step change focus moves to the task card's h2 (tabindex -1), a sound screen-reader pattern, though the polite region stays empty so a user not following focus hears nothing. The resident phone variant reorders a ranked differential with up/down buttons (SC 2.5.7) and the tablet peek sheet is 12 % with the CTA thumb-reachable. The costs are real: the stem is not visible in the peek state on tablet or phone (title and CTA only), the expanded sheet reaches 70 % on the phone and enters the central zone, the 84 px step rail squeezes P1 to about 71 % at 1920, at 4K the CTA sits far below the content in a mostly empty 400 px card, and the sharpness indicator is an unlabeled span that reduces to a bare dot at rest (A and B make it a labelled button). The linear flow will annoy free-roaming residents even with Skip to the question and the All tools switch. Product, mode and degraded states are unmistakable, the director page is a legible dashboard with an aggregate-only guard and a keyboard-path column, and the Dx-refusal variant proves the shell scales to clinical without forking. On a UX and accessibility lens this is the concept to build from.
graft_ideas: One primary action per step at the card foot, 52–56 px tall, bound to ↵; secondary actions in a smaller row beneath
'Mark without a pointer ⇧↵' as a visible button in the item card and as a tool in the rail
Honest zoom-gate rule (highest magnification reached over the focus) with the met/unmet chip
Reveal as a gate: hidden layer ACL revealOn(itemAnswered) plus refusal while a tile under the mark is stale
Calibration feedback line: 'You said Fairly sure and were right: this item comes back in 9 days'
Move focus to the task heading (h2 tabindex=-1) on step change, and also announce the step in the polite region
Publish checks that block a region item without a keyboard or text alternative
Ranked differential reordered with up/down buttons on the phone (SC 2.5.7 alternative to drag)
'Skip to the question' and an 'All tools' switch as the power-user escape hatches
Director analytics as a separate page with KPI tiles, an aggregate-only guard and a keyboard-path column in item statistics
'Fly to what you missed' in the compare-with-expert step

judges.verdict: Concept C (Task-flow) wins on the UX and accessibility lens, with B (Workbench) a close second and A (Canvas-maximal) third. C is the only concept that passed the target-size check cleanly on desktop, has the most complete dialog semantics (heading, tabs, focus trap, arrow-key radiogroup) and the clearest hierarchy for the learner: one status line, one question, one action, with the non-pointer path a first-class button. B has the best keyboard engineering and the best laptop and desktop fit (context bar, zoom-gate chip at the readout, palette as discoverability layer) and should donate those to the final design; its weakness is that the learner's item competes with a five-section dock. A is the expert's viewer and the 4K share is unmatched, but it fails focus trapping, has weak focus indication on the stepper, under-sizes its primary action on touch and hides the course shell behind edge handles; its radial, reduced-motion chip and caption-track card are the pieces worth carrying. Design notes for the plan owner regardless of winner: (1) the design-system HUD backdrop at alpha 0.62 leaves 11 px secondary lines at 3.48:1 over tissue in all three; raise the alpha or the text size; (2) chrome text has a median of 11–12 px at 4K DPR 1 in all three against the IA's 13–14 px; (3) all three hide the full Learn string below 1080 px wide although IA §7 keeps it at 1024; (4) the 'quiet' sharpness label (opacity 0) leaves a bare dot at rest, which is colour-and-shape only for sighted users; keep a low-emphasis label; (5) expanded bottom sheets exceed the 40 % rule on phones in all three and C's peek hides the stem; show the stem in the peek; (6) the ⇧R rotate/reveal conflict flagged by A's DN-A2 needs resolving in principles §4.5. Recommended final: C's flow shell and item engine, with B's context bar, zoom-gate chip, palette coverage and dialog focus model, A's radial for pen and touch, and a stem-visible peek sheet.

scores.rationale: Canvas-maximal folds regions C and D into edge handles, a 4 px step rail on the canvas top edge, a bottom-centre step card and a pointer-anchored radial, giving a 92-96 % canvas and the best 4K experience of the three. Its engine-contract map is complete and it is the only concept that renders the FR-R0 wrong-product refusal plate (launch asks Dx or Clinical-IH) with the LEARN badge kept above it. From the shell engineer's seat it is the costliest to make frame-safe: 133 non-SVG DOM nodes live inside the canvas region (step rail with tooltips, pins, handles, card, drawer, recording bar, radial), the card is a scrolling text-selectable panel over tissue re-rendered by innerHTML, and the mock measures its own height in rAF to lift the HUD; none of this is forbidden between gestures but it is the most DOM a shell must keep still, and the mock never pans or wheel-zooms, so P2 is untested rather than demonstrated. The radial takes contextmenu and a 450 ms long-press on the canvas, which needs pointer-capture arbitration against the engine's touch/pen pan start and only gets the Pencil-squeeze trigger on the native shell. It reuses none of the design-system dock/rail/bottombar components; radial menu, step rail, edge handles, step-card composite and recording bar are all net-new, so it implies the most custom work for v0.7. Accessibility is weaker in the probe: the candidates dialog does not trap focus, the confidence chips are 18 px, and under a coarse pointer the 28 px rail ticks and handles fail 44 px. The mock-only backdrop-filter on missing tiles and the CSS-blur softness must not be carried into the product. Honest about its risks (discoverability, hidden hierarchy, two new keys K and Shift+K) and about the Shift+R reveal/rotate conflict that all three inherit from the principles document.
graft_ideas: Wrong-product launch refusal plate (FR-R0 build matrix) with badge and label string kept visible above it
'Reduced motion · fly-to jumps' HUD chip that states the reduced-motion behaviour on the canvas
Director analytics (dwell heat, expert and cohort paths) drawn as engine layers over the slide rather than only as a dashboard thumbnail
Every folded surface shows its key on the handle; strip hint '? keys · Ctrl K commands'
Step card auto-summons itself on any step that carries content, so the reading surface has one fixed place
Typed zoom by pressing Enter on the magnification readout

scores.rationale: Workbench is the design system's own grid (rail, optional left panel, canvas, dock, strip) with persistent, resizable, pinnable panels and the command palette as the universal entry point, so it reuses the dock, rail, bottombar, sheet, palette, keymap, tabs, layer-row, item-card and candidate components and adds only a left panel with a keyboard-operable role=separator resizer, a one-line context bar in the banner slot, and a details-stack dock. It is the only concept whose script actually guards chrome against gestures (the resizer is deferred while .is-gesturing) and it implements cursor-anchored wheel zoom in the mock, so its P2 claim is demonstrated rather than asserted; the canvas region carries only 33 DOM nodes (HUD, navigator, context bar). Its P1 arithmetic is explicit and honest: both panels pinned at 1920 x 1080 gives 64 %, so the left panel defaults to the rail there and pins by default only from 2560 px. Panel pin/unpin changes grid tracks and resizes the canvas, which is allowed between gestures but costs a viewport resize frame; the build switch in the demo is the same attribute-flag pattern the plan forbids as a legal boundary, though B states the Learn build never carries those surfaces. The dock is a long top-down stack (player, item, expert's view, review queue, gradebook, accessibility) that reads well on 4K and 1920 but is dense, and on laptops confidence and expert's view sit one click behind the context bar. Accessibility probes are clean: focus trap holds, zero targets under 24 px, candidates answer A-F by letter, aria-keyshortcuts on the palette button, author-side deuteranopia simulation; the 24 px navigator pan buttons under touch are a design-system defect shared with C. One keymap note: the dock key I collides with map A's I (identity panel) if the shell is shared with the clinical builds. It shows v1 features (spaced-retrieval queue, Anki, CME claim, exam timer) now, tagged DB-7, which is fine for settling the dock rhythm but must be hidden at v0.7. The least distinctive of the three; the context bar and the palette groups are the parts worth stealing.
graft_ideas: Build on the design-system grid with a stated P1 arithmetic table per viewport and a pin-by-default threshold (2560 px) instead of inventing new regions
Panel resizers as role=separator with arrow-key resizing, deferred while .is-gesturing
Context bar in the banner slot when the dock folds (step, stem, zoom gate, Commit, text alternative) so the prompt is never lost on laptops
Palette groups (Panels, Layout, Fly to candidates, Settings) with aria-keyshortcuts on the visible search button
Expert's view block with learner-vs-expert time-to-first-zoom and dwell numbers after reveal
Layer rows that print the ACL (revealOn(itemAnswered), authorOnly) and provenance line
Gradebook status line 'Posted within 60 s (AGS)' with the xAPI statement list

scores.rationale: Task-flow turns region C into a step rail (Open, Screen, Examine, Decide, Complete) that discloses tools per phase and region D into a task card that always ends in one 56 px primary action; on laptops the card closes and a one-line task bar keeps step, stem and CTA visible, on tablets and phones the rail becomes a flow bar and the card a peek sheet (title plus CTA) above the central zone. The learner's top task is the fastest and safest here: readiness check (streaming or pack, link, captions, keys), gate box reporting the highest magnification reached over the focus, Skip to the question, confidence that feeds the queue not the grade, reveal as an ACL gate, grades queued when offline, and the resident variant with button-reordered differential (SC 2.5.7). Engineering-wise the canvas region stays lean (40 DOM nodes), the task bar is contained (contain: layout paint style), the OS reduced-motion query is honoured and fly-to becomes a cut, the canvas aria-label updates with magnification, and every CTA maps to one command id, which is the cleanest command-bus story of the three. Three feasibility flags: the shell is one DOM switched by html[data-product] across all four builds, which as shipped would be exactly the runtime flag plan 12 section 2 rules out, so the final must compile per product and keep C's flow as shared components; 'will not reveal while a tile under the mark is stale' needs a per-ROI settle query that the quality record (per-frame NTF) does not provide, so it is an FR- backlog item on geometry services; and per-phase tool disclosure requires a phase-aware allowlist in the module schema and the command registry. P1 passes at 1920 x 1080 by 0.3 points with the 84 px rail docked, so there is no margin for widening, and the expanded sheet on tablets intrudes on the central zone (DN-C5, honest). The page is the heaviest (6.6k nodes, 90 inline SVGs) but most of that is demo variants and the director dashboard. Accessibility probes are clean (focus trap, zero small targets at 24 px, tabs with arrow keys in the candidates dialog, caption region aria-live=off); the Tier chip at 24 px and the shared navigator pan buttons fail 44 px under touch. The LMS host frame and the cookieless Platform Storage note make it the only mock that is reviewed in its real iframe context.
