judges.verdict: From the shell-and-engine lens: Concept C (Task-flow) wins on balance (47/60) because it makes the learner's top task fastest, has the best tablet and phone story, and maps every live element onto a contract, with three items to fix before it is the MVP shell: build it per product rather than switching html[data-product], file a per-ROI tile-settle query against geometry services for the 'no reveal on a stale tile' rule, and add a phase-aware tool allowlist to the module schema; P1 at 1920 must be re-checked once the step rail's width is final. Concept B (Workbench, 42/60) is the most buildable shell as drawn: it reuses the design-system grid, adds the fewest custom components, keeps only 33 DOM nodes over the canvas and is the only mock that guards chrome against gestures, so the final design should carry C's flow on B's grid mechanics (pin thresholds, gesture-guarded resizers, context bar when the dock folds). Concept A (Canvas-maximal, 41/60) is the most distinctive and the best on a 4K display, but it is the costliest to make frame-safe (133 DOM nodes over the canvas, radial and long-press arbitration with the engine's pointer model, no design-system region reuse, no pan or zoom in the mock), and it has the accessibility defects (focus trap, 18 px chips, 28 px touch targets); take its refusal plate, reduced-motion HUD chip and analytics-as-layers idea. Design notes for the plan owner: the Shift+R reveal-versus-rotate conflict is in the principles document, not the concepts; the design-system navigator pan buttons are 24 px under touch; B's I key collides with the clinical identity panel if the shell is shared.

synthesis.summary: Wrote the final education-module screen wsi-viewer/design/screens/final/education-module.html (314 KB, self-contained, links ../../design-system/tokens.css and base.css by relative path, no network). Base is concept C (Task-flow: phase rail Open→Screen→Examine→Decide→Complete with per-phase tools, one 56 px primary action per step bound to Enter, graded/practice/CME/ungraded card header, honest zoom gate with half-credit rule, readiness check, coverage %, reveal as layer-ACL gate refused on stale tiles, review queue only in Complete, 'Fly to what you missed', resident ranked differential with up/down buttons, record-a-tour, Dx-refused clinical variant). Grafts from B: context bar when the card folds (as a grid row under the top bar, not DOM over the canvas), zoom-gate chip beside the magnification readout, candidates dialog focus model (h2, tabs, focus-trapped arrow-key radiogroup, Enter commits, Escape returns focus to the canvas), one-sentence assertive reveal announcement, keyboard-resizable dock (role=separator, 320–520, deferred while gesturing), palette coverage with aria-keyshortcuts, publish lint, IoU histogram + n≥30 item stats + keyboard-path column. Grafts from A: Focus mode (Shift+K; labelled edge handles + caption-track card at bottom centre, desktop ≥1600 only), radial at the pointer (right-click/long-press/squeeze, Esc closes, clamped to the canvas), 'Not in this build' palette group with the Learn refusal microcopy, wrong-product launch refusal plate (FR-R0) with the badge kept above, 'Reduced motion · fly-to jumps' HUD chip, cohort analytics as layers on the real slide. Judge-measured fixes applied: rail 64 px (80 at 4K) and card 320 px (440 at 4K) so P1 has margin (measured 73.2 % at 1920×1080 with the LMS frame, 83.0 % at 4K); 44 px phase and navigator pan buttons under a coarse pointer; sheet peek shows title+stem+CTA on tablets and a 64 px stem+CTA bar on phones (74.8 % canvas); expanded sheets capped at 40 % on tablets and phones (measured 36.6 % / 40.0 %), landscape uses the side drawer; CTA follows content on pointer surfaces and is pinned on touch sheets; seeded non-lattice H&E tissue (dense lymphocyte cortex, mantle/germinal-centre follicles, sinus histiocytes, capsule, cohesive nest of large vesicular-nucleus tumour cells; DAB recolour for CK AE1/AE3) with the default 20× view on the nest edge so the mark and the sinus are both visible; HUD backdrop 0.78 and 12 px secondary lines; sharpness label kept at low emphasis (never a bare dot); Shift+R reveal/rotate conflict resolved by moving reveal to U. Demo strip kept (product, audience, step, item, network, device, launch-asks-for, tile errors, Dx refused, gradebook fails, LTI failed, LMS frame, reduced motion, 44 px, light chrome, CVD, focus mode, radial, live markers, guides) plus URL-hash presets; collapsed 'Design decisions' section lists sources per element, the judges' disagreements and resolutions, the engine-contract map, the measured P1 table and design notes DF-1..DF-8. Screenshots at the six required viewports plus 15 state shots are in wsi-viewer/design/screens/final/shots/; a Playwright keyboard-path test (Shift+Enter → arrows → Enter commits → U reveals with assertive sentence → N/Shift+N → K → Shift+K → Ctrl+K 'dx' refusal → Shift+R rotates) passes with no console errors, and the DOM measurement reports no central-zone intruders and no targets under 24 px at any of the six viewports.
notes: Measured canvas share at rest (app frame, LMS host bar on, review chrome excluded): 3840×2160 83.0 %, 1920×1080 73.2 %, 1440×900 80.6 %, 1366×1024 82.0 %, 1024×1366 72.8 % (180 px peek), 390×844 74.8 % (64 px peek). No HUD item, navigator, sheet or drawer intersects the central 50 % zone at rest; no target under 24 px at any viewport; 44 px targets under a coarse pointer.

Design notes for the plan owner (also in the page's Design decisions section): DF-1 reveal is now U, Shift+R stays rotate (principles §4.5 to amend; Learn additions become N, Shift+N, Space, Shift+Enter, U, Shift+E, K, Shift+K); DF-2 region C is a step/tool rail (64/80 px) and the module schema needs a phase-aware tool allowlist; DF-3 'no reveal on a stale tile' needs a per-ROI settle query on geometry services (FR backlog); DF-4 Tier chip shown as information in Learn, owner to confirm; DF-5 HUD backdrop 0.78, 12 px HUD secondary text, 14 px chrome body at 4K and --target-driven navigator pan buttons should move into tokens.css/base.css; DF-6 base.css allows 60 vh phone sheets while this screen caps at 40 %; DF-7 last step is a completion marker, AGS posts per item; DF-8 mock liberties (seeded SVG tissue, CSS blur for soft, DOM overlays, Machado deutan matrix).

Judge disagreements resolved as recorded in the page: 4K docked by default with A's layout as Focus mode; B's context-bar content on C's grid-row mechanics; linear flow kept with escape hatches; peek shows the stem, expanded sheets ≤ 40 % everywhere, landscape = side drawer; CTA follows content on pointer surfaces and is pinned on touch; product switch is review-only (separate build per product, stated in About and the decisions section).

The product/mode variants (Learn, Viewer RUO, Clinical-IH consult, Dx refused/active) and audiences (undergraduate, medical student, resident unknown, CME) remain switchable from the demo strip; URL-hash presets (e.g. #view=director, #item=revealed, #focus=1, #cand=1, #launch=dx, #aud=res&peek=0) drive the screenshot script.

Review tooling (not part of the deliverable) is in the scratchpad: <scratch>/final-edu/shoot.mjs (six viewports with P1/target measurement), states.mjs (15 state shots), kbtest.mjs (keyboard path and sheet caps), polite.mjs (live-region trace). No git commands were run.

Known limitations: the tissue is a wireframe stand-in (procedural patterns), not scanner pixels; the fuzzy palette matcher is substring-first; the clinical and RUO cards are proofs that the flow shell does not fork, not the owning screens.

scores.rationale: Canvas-maximal gives the expert annotator the largest working area (84 % at 1920×1080 measured, more at 4K) and the HUD tool line plus one-key drawers (I/K/⇧K/U/⇧E) make the draw–classify loop fast once learned; the pin-chrome escape hatch reusing the same dock element is a cheap, honest answer to the discoverability risk the concept itself names. Clarity suffers from the top-left stack of three small HUD lines (tool line, first-run hint, LOD notice) at 10–12 px that do not scale at 3840×2160 (no 4K shot was shipped; the one I rendered is hard to read), from the drawer tab bar wrapping into two rows at 360 px, and from the legend HUD occluding tissue, including the selected tumour polygon at 1024×1366. Accessibility is the weak lens: the 11 legend buttons are 22 px tall (SC 2.5.8 fail, stacked so no spacing exception) and carry role=listitem, which removes their button semantics; the keymap declares aria-modal=true but does not trap focus; the tool wheel opens dead-centre over the slide and its only keyboard twin is 'the keys themselves'; the tablet sheet covers the scale bar and magnification (confirmed by measurement). Positives: Esc returns focus to the canvas, the curtain handle is a keyboard-operable slider, the live regions are pre-populated, every sampled string is above 5:1 and motion tokens zero under reduced-motion. Feasibility is high because the chrome is thin, the drawer is absolutely positioned (no canvas re-layout) and the wheel/legend are declared GPU layers; degraded states (Soft, tile retry with a Retry button, W60 channel cap explained per row) are the most complete of the three. Device fit is uneven: phone is excellent and minimal, tablet drawing is routed through a long-press wheel rather than visible pen tools, and 4K is unaddressed beyond a wider drawer.
graft_ideas: Tool wheel at the pen tip / right-click with the class ring in the centre (Q, 1–9), as a transient GPU layer
HUD tool line that states what the next click will do: active tool + key, active class + swatch, undo depth
Class legend with per-class counts, detection-layer totals and LOD state, click-a-class-to-jump
First-run hint line retired by the telemetry commandInvoked event rather than a coach-mark tour
Pin-chrome escape hatch that turns the transient drawer into the classic rail + dock without a second implementation
Per-channel 'cap reached on this device class' explanations in the multiplex panel and a Retry button in the tile-error strip state

scores.rationale: The Workbench is the most complete answer to US-R1/R2/R3 for long desktop sessions: Library (cohort, slides with coverage bars, layers) and Context (inspector with geometry, QuPath GeoJSON properties, model jobs with a 'Retry at 8-bit tier' failure path, channels, export with byte-identity) each have a fixed home, and the always-visible palette field indexes commands, slides, layers and classes so the keymap is learned by use. Hierarchy and labelling are clear and the product/mode story is strong: full RUO string, H&E/CC0 chips, and a Dx-refusal banner at the top edge with role=status that also reaches the assertive live region. The costs are canvas share (68 % measured at 1920×1080, 61 % with the Library pinned) and density: five Context tabs crowd at 320 px, the laptop panel strip uses rotated vertical text, and the touch bottom bar is eight icon-only 44 px buttons with no visible labels. Accessibility has real strengths (keyboard-resizable dock separators with aria-valuenow, roving arrow keys across tabs, a keyboard-operable curtain slider, focus-mode '\') and real defects: aria-modal=true on the keymap with no focus trap and focus dropping to body on Esc, aria-selected on plain buttons in the panel strip, two role=listitem buttons, 27 hover-only title tooltips, and a pen hint rendered inside the central 50 % on tablets. Feasibility is good because dock widths are fixed grid tracks so panel re-renders never re-lay out the canvas, and the compare gutter is a 1 px chrome track. Device fit is the best-balanced of the three on paper (4K both docks, laptop drawers plus panel strip, portrait sheets, phone at 80 % canvas, a convincing 1200×640 widget), held back only by the unlabelled touch bar.
graft_ideas: Always-visible search/palette field in the top bar that indexes commands, slides, layers, classes and bookmarks and shows every shortcut
Keyboard-resizable docks as role=separator with aria-valuemin/max/now and 16 px arrow steps
Inspector showing selected-object geometry (area, perimeter, nuclei inside, mean p) and the QuPath GeoJSON properties with the 'RGB restored on export' note
Slide-tray coverage bars from the engine's visibleCoverage service
Laptop panel strip so every Context panel stays one click away when the dock is a drawer
Dx-refusal banner at the top canvas edge with role=status mirrored into the assertive live region
Failed-job remediation rows ('worker out of memory · Retry at 8-bit tier') in the model panel

scores.rationale: Task-flow organises the workspace around the cohort loop a computational pathologist actually runs (Open → Screen → Examine → Annotate → Export, 'Slide 14 of 48 · 3 done', candidate-region queue with Fly there and reviewed marks, a single primary action per step ending in 'Mark slide complete'), and the all-steps toggle and global keys keep the steps from becoming gates; the stated cost is one click between Examine and Annotate and channels sitting one level deeper for the spatial-biology persona. Hierarchy is the strongest of the three (eyebrow, title, purpose, footer action) and product/mode is unmistakable across RUO, Clinical-IH (purpose chip, accession, label image, QA chip, not-validated marker) and the launch-refused plate; the misses are the full RUO string disappearing at exactly 1024 px portrait (the container-query bug A documented and fixed), 9–10 px key hints, and a measured 66 % canvas at 1920×1080 against a claimed 71 %. It is the best concept under the accessibility lens: real listboxes with Tab/Space, a radiogroup class picker with keys 1–8, the curtain as a native range input (SC 2.5.7), keymap and About as in-panel non-modal overlays that never cover the slide and return focus to the canvas, a canvas aria-label that updates with the step, a sheet grab button with aria-expanded that works from the keyboard, 44 px tools and rows under pointer: coarse, deutan and protan simulation applied to swatches as well as the canvas, and a user reduce-motion toggle. Remaining gaps are small: 18 px CVD segmented buttons, a 20 px sheet handle, a 30 px-wide phone search button, an empty polite live region at load, and no focus trap (though none is claimed). Feasibility is sound (one step registry drives rail, bottom bar, tray, panel, footer and aria-label; the laptop drawer is absolutely positioned) with one caveat: the in-flow sheet changes canvas height on expand, which is a user-invoked re-layout between gestures and must stay out of the gesture path. Device fit is the most considered: it is the only concept that scales rail, panel and body text at 4K, the pen variant shows labelled 44 px tools and a pen-tip palette, portrait yields height instead of covering the slide, and the phone keeps the sharpness state in the HUD, at the price of the lowest phone canvas share at rest (64 % measured).
graft_ideas: Step registry that drives rail, bottom bar, tool tray, panel, footer action and the canvas aria-label from one source
Candidate-region queue with 'Fly there' buttons and reviewed marks, reusing the Learn keyboard-alternative pattern as the SC 2.5.7 path for screening
Curtain position as a native range input beside the canvas divider

In-flow peeking sheet below 1080 px so the canvas yields height rather than being covered, with a keyboard-operable grab button
Deuteranopia and protanopia simulation applied to palette swatches as well as the canvas, with the ΔE00 guarantee stated in the panel
4K scaling rule: rail 112, panel 460, body 14 px so chrome stays legible at DPR 1

judges.verdict: Winner under the UX and accessibility lens: research-annotation-c (Task-flow), by a clear margin on accessibility and device fit and level with B on workflow fit and clarity. C is the only concept whose keyboard, pen and touch paths were designed together (native range for the curtain, radiogroup class picker, listboxes with Space-to-fly, non-modal in-panel keymap, aria-expanded sheet, 44 px coarse-pointer targets, 4K text scaling) and whose state communication (step eyebrow, single primary action, RUO/Clinical-IH/Dx variants, launch-refused plate, honest sharpness strip) is readable without hovering. B (Workbench) is the strongest desktop power-user shell and should donate its palette field, keyboard-resizable separators, inspector and laptop panel strip; A (Canvas-maximal) is the boldest idea but fails SC 2.5.8 on its legend, misuses role=listitem on buttons, declares a modal it does not trap, occludes tissue with its HUD legend and sheet, and does not scale at 4K, so it should donate the tool wheel, HUD tool line, legend counts and the pin-chrome escape hatch rather than be the base. Fixes required of the winner before the final screen: restore the full RUO string at ≥ 1024 px (container-query bug D-A7), bring the CVD segmented control, sheet handle and phone search button to 24/44 px, pre-populate the polite live region at load, keep the sheet-expand re-layout out of the gesture path, and add 44 px navigator pan buttons on touch in base.css (a defect shared by all three).

scores.rationale: Geometry is the most engine-friendly of the three: the single drawer is position:absolute over the canvas edge so the WebGL canvas never resizes when a panel opens, the page declares zero CSS transitions, and the probe found no element with motion under prefers-reduced-motion; canvas share measured 92 % at 1920, 96 % at 4K (I rendered the missing 4K shot), 87 % phone, 88 % tablet. Every command goes through one run() dispatcher and the palette (45 commands with keys), keymap and tool wheel read from it, which is the command-bus shape plan 04 §8 wants, and the data-live map (62 markers) covers state document, layer API, annotation API, event bus, launch context, telemetry and the proposed commandInvoked event. The mock's own shell discipline is the weakest, though: each command calls render() which rebuilds the whole chrome, so a zoom burst produced 304 chrome mutations, 44 root-class toggles (renderZoom flips a class on the app root per magnification change) and 4 layout-shift entries, versus 31 textContent updates for C; this is exactly the pattern a thin TypeScript shell over the engine must not use. It also writes state into the URL with history.replaceState on every command, which inside anywidget (same document as JupyterLab) or an iframe mutates the host's URL. More of its UI lives as interactive DOM over the canvas than the other concepts (legend panel with 11 buttons, HUD tool line buttons, tool wheel, compare bar, curtain handle), so the product owes the most custom GPU-layer work, and the legend rows are 22 px tall: 11 targets under 24 px on desktop and tablet, the only concept failing SC 2.5.8 at rest. Seven new bindings (K, ⇧K, U, ⇧E, ⇧G, ⇧V, backtick) plus the K/⇧H clash with the component sheet add registry churn, and 116 page-defined classes (about 95 product-facing: radial, legend-hud, compare-bar, panes, drawer modes) sit outside base.css. The transient-drawer model also means the layers list, which annotators keep open all day, occludes tissue when open and hides the bottom HUD under the sheet on tablet and phone. The inline typed-zoom field, the quality sheet behind the sharpness indicator and the channel-cap reason text on W60 are the right patterns and should be kept whichever concept wins.
graft_ideas: Inline typed-zoom input on the magnification readout (× or µm/px) instead of prompt()
Quality sheet behind the sharpness indicator showing NTF %, resolution deficit and link state from the telemetry record
Tool wheel at the pen tip / long-press / right-click as a user-invoked GPU layer, with letters as the keyboard twin
Class legend with per-class counts and detection totals plus click-to-jump, but as a 24 px-row dock section or collapsible HUD, not a 22 px panel over the canvas
Pin-chrome (backtick) toggle that turns transient drawers into the classic rail+dock layout with one implementation
First-run HUD hint line retired by the commandInvoked telemetry event
Channel rows that state the device-class cap reason when a channel cannot be enabled on W60/phone
Strip notice priority order (transient > error > Dx > tiler) as a documented rule

scores.rationale: From the shell-engineering lens this is the most buildable MVP: docks are fixed grid tracks whose widths are CSS custom properties, the resizers are focusable separators that change one variable (arrow keys, 16 px steps) and add the base.css is-gesturing class to zero every transition while dragging, so panel work never touches the canvas during a gesture; at 1080–1599 both docks become absolute drawers over the canvas edge and the Context tabs survive as a 36 px panel strip. It reuses the design system most heavily (101 page-defined classes, the fewest, and the shortest script at 320 lines), proposes only two new bindings (backslash focus mode, ⇧G) and keeps Ctrl to K only, Alt and F-keys ignored, which satisfies the Hyperdrive rule by construction. One registry (50 entries covering commands, panels, slides, classes, layers and bookmarks) drives the always-visible search field, the keys and the panel buttons, and the keymap sheet shows presets with reserved keys greyed. The contract map is complete (66 markers) and the Inspector is the best mapping of plan 04 §8 GeometryService and the QuPath adapter: area, perimeter, nuclei inside, detections inside, mean p, raw GeoJSON properties with the colour-remap note; the Model tab maps aiResultArrived/Accepted/Rejected and the uncertainty queue, and the widget is the same shell with docks removed. The caveat is that zoom and pan are not simulated at all, so the probe's zero mutations during the gesture burst prove nothing; P2 is asserted by architecture, not demonstrated. Docks as grid tracks at ≥1600 px resize the WebGL canvas on every open/close (allowed between gestures, but each is a swapchain resize and tile refetch), pinning the Library at 1920 drops the canvas to 58–61 % below P1, and the pen hint callout sits in the central zone on tablet portrait. Targets: one under 24 px (the 6 px resizer, which has the keyboard path), phone 0 under 24. Clarity and completeness are bought with chrome, which is the honest trade the rationale states.
graft_ideas: Search field in the top bar as the command palette entry point (Ctrl K), indexing commands, slides, layers, classes and bookmarks with shortcuts shown
Panel strip: Context tab labels stay visible as a 36 px column when the dock collapses at laptop width
Count badges on rail panel icons (3 slides, 5 layers) so state is readable with panels closed
Keyboard-resizable dock separators implemented as CSS custom properties with is-gesturing zeroing transitions
Inspector block: geometry-service values (area, perimeter, nuclei inside, detections inside, mean p) plus raw GeoJSON properties with the on-screen colour remap note
Model jobs list with per-job provenance and the 'worker out of memory (16-bit tiles) → Retry at 8-bit tier' recovery action
Viewed-coverage bar per slide in the tray from the engine's visibleCoverage service
Canvas-share readout per surface as a CI assertion for P1

scores.rationale: This concept demonstrates the gesture discipline the plan requires rather than asserting it: it binds wheel on the canvas with passive:false and a pointer-anchored zoom (the FR-V1 shape), sets is-gesturing on drag, skips its 120 ms fly-to tween under reduced motion, and during the probe's burst every chrome rect stayed byte-identical while the only non-HUD chrome mutations were 31 textContent updates to the LOD label; HUD, navigator and strip updated by textContent and style only, and the live region is debounced to settle. Its contract map is the richest (76 markers) and goes beyond the others with geometry:visibleCoverage, events:displayQaStatus, telemetry:switch, export jobs and the Clinical-IH/Dx identity fields, and its degraded-state set is the fullest (cold 4G, offline with and without pack, tile errors keeping the ancestor with a Retry chip, server slow, soft level, Tier 2, GPU reset, manifest and launch-refused plates) with §5 strings verbatim. The cost is custom component work: 133 page-defined classes (about 118 product-facing: step rail, step bar, step tray, five step panels, in-flow sheet with grab handle, panel overlays, pen palette, flow chips), the widget variant is a second DOM copy of the top bar, rail and canvas rather than the same component in a compact mode, and the step/progress state ('Slide 14 of 48 · 3 done') needs a new research-package store that is not an engine contract (correctly flagged in C-1). The in-flow sheet on tablet and phone keeps the centre uncovered but changes the canvas height on every expand/collapse, which is a WebGL resize and tile refetch, and on W60 that is a dropped frame each time; the overlay sheets of A and B avoid it. The typed zoom uses prompt(), which sandboxed iframes without allow-modals suppress, and the probe logged 23 small layout-shift entries from HUD readouts changing width, so readouts need reserved widths. Canvas share is at the P1 floor at 1920 (71 %) and on phone (70 %, four chrome bands), and three segmented controls plus the 20 px sheet grab handle are under 24 px. Only three new bindings (N, ⇧N, backslash) and N shared with Learn keep the registry clean.
graft_ideas: The canvas input pattern as shell code: pointer-anchored wheel with preventDefault, is-gesturing on pointerdown/up, HUD updated by textContent only, live region announced at settle (500 ms debounce)
Reserve fixed widths (tabular numerals, min-width) for magnification, scale-bar and position readouts so text updates never produce layout shifts
Export step: target checklist (GeoJSON QuPath dialect, DICOM ANN, patches+labels, region OME-TIFF), manifest preview, jobs with byte-identity badge, Cancel and Download
Strip Retry chip for tile errors and the complete §6 state inventory with verbatim microcopy, including GPU-reset and launch-refused plates
Keymap and About as in-dock panel overlays that never cover the slide, with the preset selector and reserved keys greyed
Candidate regions R1–R4 as a real list with Fly there and Space to fly, reused by Learn's region-marking alternative
Flow chip 'Slide 14 of 48 · 3 done' and a per-step primary footer action (Next / Mark slide complete) driven by the collection store
Pen-tip tool palette on Pencil squeeze as a transient GPU layer

judges.verdict: Engineering verdict: Concept B (Workbench) is the strongest base for the MVP shell. It is the thinnest layer over the engine contracts and the design system (fewest custom classes, fixed grid tracks with CSS-variable resizing, one command registry driving search field, keys and buttons, two new bindings, same shell for the Jupyter widget) and it already maps GeometryService, the QuPath adapter, the layer provenance tuple and the aiResult events in the places users will look. Its one gap is that P2 is asserted rather than demonstrated; Concept C (Task-flow) is the one that measurably holds chrome geometry fixed during a zoom burst (31 textContent mutations, no rect changes) with a pointer-anchored wheel handler and settle-debounced announcements, so its canvas input pattern, export step, state inventory and in-dock keymap/About overlays should be grafted into B. Concept A (Canvas-maximal) has the most engine-friendly geometry (constant canvas size, no transitions, 92–96 % canvas) and the most ideas worth stealing (inline typed zoom, quality sheet, pin-chrome toggle, legend with counts, tool wheel), but its mock shell rebuilds the whole chrome on every command (304 chrome mutations and 44 root-class toggles per zoom burst), writes state into the URL on every command (embed-hostile), places interactive 22 px DOM over the canvas (fails SC 2.5.8) and implies the most custom GPU-layer work and the largest discoverability risk. Design notes for the plan owner: docks as grid tracks (B at ≥1600, C at ≥1600) and C's in-flow sheet resize the WebGL canvas between gestures, which costs a frame on W60 and should be measured against NFR-P9; "Run model on ROI" in all three concepts is a research-package job service, not an engine contract, and belongs on the v0.9 backlog; and no concept may ship URL-hash state or prompt() inside anywidget or an iframe.

scores.rationale: As a keyboard-first reader this is the concept I would reach for on a 4K display: 93 % canvas at 1920 and 96 % at 4K, a top-left HUD line that says what the next click does (tool, class, undo depth, LOD), and a class legend with live counts that answers 'what is on this slide' without opening a panel. Every drawer is one key and the backtick pin collapses it into the classic three-column layout, so the expert path is fast. But for the persona's actual job here, annotating a cohort for hours and reviewing model output, the chrome is hidden when I need it most: the annotation list, layer rows and job progress live in a transient drawer that covers 360 px of tissue (verified: the canvas rect does not change when K opens, so it occludes rather than pushes), and there is no slide progress, coverage or 'done' state anywhere, which is the wrong-slide/missed-area gap I care about most. Safety and mode: RUO badge and string are correct, but the Clinical-IH variant shows a 'Research session · RUO' purpose chip that is not one of Design note D1's four fixed strings (flag as Design note), and the keymap dialog is centred over the canvas (980 × 499 at 1920, covers the canvas centre), which fails P1's 'including dialogs' test. Accessibility is the weakest of the three on measurement: the 11 legend rows are 22 px high at every viewport (SC 2.5.8 fails on desktop and badly on touch), the HUD tool/class buttons stay 24 px on tablet where 44 px is required, the bottom sheet covers the scale bar and magnification on tablet and phone, drawer tab key hints are still shown on the phone sheet, and the tool wheel's only keyboard twin is 'the keys themselves'. Feasibility is good: overlay drawer, textContent HUD, GPU wheel and curtain all respect P2, and the pinned mode is the design system's dock. Device fit suffers on tablet (legend overlaps tissue at 1024 portrait, sheet hides HUD) and in the widget, where the drawer eats a third of a 1200 × 640 cell. Fatigue-wise it is the quietest screen of the three, and the W60 channel-cap explanation ('Channel cap reached (4 on this device class) — hide another channel to enable') is the most honest degraded state in the set.
graft_ideas: HUD tool line (active tool + key, active class swatch, undo depth, detection LOD state) as the collapsed-chrome toolbar; both items are 24 px buttons so pointer users are never stranded
Class legend as a HUD under the navigator with annotation counts and detection class totals; click-a-class jumps to its first object
Per-device-class channel cap rows that say why the fifth channel cannot be enabled on W60/phones, and the '8-bit preview tier while moving · 16-bit at settle' line in the strip
Pin/unpin chrome as the single escape hatch between canvas-maximal and classic dock (same dock element, no second implementation)
First-run HUD hint line that disappears after the first command (telemetry commandInvoked decides), never a modal tour
Tool wheel at the pointer / pen squeeze as a user-invoked GPU layer exempt from the central-50 % rule, with Q turning it into the class ring (1–9)

scores.rationale: This is the bench I would actually sit at for a 200-slide annotation session: Library (what am I looking at) and Context (what is selected, what can I do) have fixed homes that never swap sides, so muscle memory survives across surfaces, and the always-visible palette field (Ctrl+K: 'heat', 'ck', 'stroma', 'export' each reach a toggle, a slide, a class and a panel; '40 of 53' rows) teaches the keymap by use. Its panel content is the most complete and the most useful to a pathologist: the Inspector shows area, perimeter, nuclei inside, detections inside and mean p for the selected polygon plus the QuPath GeoJSON properties verbatim; the Model tab has run-on-ROI, a failed job with 'Retry at 8-bit tier' and an uncertainty queue reviewed with Space; Channels has histograms, auto-window p1–p99 and reset-to-omero; Compare shows the registration residual (affine · VALIS · 3.1 µm). The Slides tray carries a coverage bar from the geometry service, which is the one missed-area guard in the set besides C's. Clarity is strong (RUO badge, string, counts on the collapsed rail icons, §5 strings verbatim in the degraded states), but two things fail the plan's own tests: the keymap dialog is centred over the canvas (880 × 484, covers the centre point, P1 'including dialogs'), and on tablet the pen hint HUD (318 × 72) sits inside the central 50 % of the canvas. The chrome appetite is real and honestly reported: 72 % at 1920 with the Library collapsed, 58 % with it pinned, and a 56 % laptop canvas if the annotation list stays open; the 1440 panel strip and focus mode (89 %) are the mitigations and they work. Accessibility measures well on desktop (only the 6 px resizers are under 24 px, and they are keyboard separators), but on touch the bottom bar is eight unlabelled icons, the pan buttons stay 24 px (a base.css defect shared by all three), the sheet covers the scale bar and magnification, and the phone offline variant shows no offline text, only the sharpness dot. Feasibility is clean: dock widths are grid tracks so a panel re-render never re-lays out the canvas, compare is a state not a screen, and the widget is the same shell with docks removed. Device fit is best at 4K and 1920 and weakest on tablet/phone, which matters because the persona consults on an iPad.
graft_ideas: Two-dock split with fixed homes (Library: cohort/slides/layers; Context: inspector/annotations/model/channels/export) and count badges on the rail switchers when a dock is collapsed
Always-visible palette field in the top bar as the discoverability layer, indexing commands, slides, layers, classes and bookmarks with shortcuts shown
Inspector card for the selected annotation: µm geometry, nuclei/detections inside, mean model probability, GeoJSON (QuPath dialect) properties verbatim, Fly to (Space)

Model tab: region segmented control (viewport / selected annotation / whole slide), tile and time estimate, job list with failure recovery ('Retry at 8-bit tier'), uncertainty queue with 'Review next (Space)' and 'Export queue as labels'
Channels panel with per-channel histogram, 16-bit tag, auto-window (p1–p99) and reset-to-omero; channel grid view (⇧G)
Compare bar with lock / affine / none, 'B follows A', curtain, and the registration method + residual in µm; the second view's magnification readout says 'linked'
Laptop panel strip: vertical tab names stay visible when the Context dock collapses so completeness survives the drawer
Visible-area coverage bar in the slide tray, driven by the geometry service

scores.rationale: This is the concept that takes wrong-slide and missed-area risk seriously: 'Slide 14 of 48 · 3 done' sits in the top bar at every width, the Open step's cohort list has To do / In progress / Done chips, the Screen step shows coverage (62 %), an HPF grid and 'Next candidate', and the Export footer ends with 'Mark slide complete (N)', so a resident working a 48-slide set cannot lose their place; that is exactly what I would want when teaching annotation. Product and mode are the most unmistakable of the three: the Clinical-IH variant uses a D1-conformant purpose chip ('QA review · blinded'), accession, label image in the navigator, NAV indicator and the QA chip; the launch-refused plate opens nothing; the Dx refusal string is verbatim; the CVD simulation recolours the whole canvas and the swatches, not just the overlays. It also honours P1 where A and B do not: the keymap is a panel overlay (359 × 926, replaces the dock, never touches the slide) and the palette anchors under the Commands field, and on tablet the step sheet is in-flow, so the canvas shrinks from 960 to 510 px rather than being covered and the scale bar and magnification stay visible (verified in the headless pass). The cost is the step metaphor itself: Examine and Annotate interleave constantly in real annotation, the rail's tools change with the step (a muscle-memory tax even though keys stay global), multiplex is a section inside Examine, and the palette's 'export' search returned only 'Go to step 5 · Export' and 'Submit export', not the direct GeoJSON/DICOM ANN commands B exposes. All-steps mode fixes most of this, but then C is a conventional dock with a progress rail, and that is the mode an expert would live in. Accessibility is the strongest in practice (labelled 44 px tool tray, real listboxes, radiogroup class picker with 1–8, canvas aria-label updated per step, reduced-motion toggle), with small misses: the CVD segmented control is 18 px high, the sheet grab handle is 20 px on touch, keyboard hints are shown on the phone sheet, and the measured phone canvas share was 64 % against the claimed 71 %. Feasibility is slightly lower than A/B because the in-flow sheet resizes the canvas (allowed between gestures but a resize path the engine must own), one registry must drive rail, panel, footer and aria-label together, and all-steps is a second layout to keep in sync. Device fit is the best in the set: one IA scales from 4K (82 %) to the phone without a second information architecture, and the pen-tip palette plus 'finger pans · pen draws' is shown on the tablet variants.
graft_ideas: Cohort progress scaffolding: 'Slide N of M · k done' in the top bar, To do / In progress / Done filter chips in the slide list, and a 'Mark slide complete' action as the export step's terminal command
Coverage % plus HPF grid and 'Next candidate' as the screening-step guard against missed areas
Keymap as a panel overlay that replaces the dock, never a dialog over the canvas; palette anchored under the top-bar search field, outside the central 50 %
In-flow peeking sheet on tablet/phone that pushes the canvas rather than covering it, so the scale bar and magnification stay visible with the sheet expanded
Whole-canvas deuteranopia/protanopia simulation that also recolours the swatches and legend
Clinical-IH / Dx variants with the D1 purpose chip, accession, label image in the navigator and the fixed not-validated marker, so the same research screen demonstrates every build's labelling
Export step with explicit targets (GeoJSON, DICOM ANN, patches + labels, OME-TIFF region), a manifest preview, and jobs with DONE / RUNNING / QUEUED plus the byte-identity badge
Canvas aria-label that names the slide, magnification and current step, driven by the same registry as the rail and footer

judges.verdict: Narrow win for research-annotation-c (46) over research-annotation-b (45), with research-annotation-a (43) as the HUD donor. From the sign-out pathologist's chair the deciding factor is safety on a cohort: C is the only concept that keeps 'which slide, how many done, how much of this slide have I seen, and is it finished' on screen at every width, and it is the only one whose keymap, palette and tablet sheet never cover the slide centre (A and B both centre the keymap dialog over the canvas, failing P1's 'including dialogs' test; B's tablet pen hint sits in the central zone). B is the better desktop bench for a long expert session (fixed panel homes, always-visible palette, the richest Inspector/Model/Channels/Compare content, coverage bar) and I would refuse C's step-locked tool rail as a daily driver unless all-steps mode is the default for experts on ≥1920 displays; so the final design should be C's IA and responsive geometry with all-steps as the expert default, B's panel content and two-dock discipline inside it, and A's HUD tool line and counted legend as the collapsed-chrome mode. Design notes to carry forward: A's 'Research session · RUO' purpose chip is not one of D1's four strings; the navigator pan buttons (24 px) and the phone badge (34 × 24) are below the coarse-pointer target size in the shared base.css for all three concepts; C's CVD segmented control (18 px) and A's legend rows (22 px) fail SC 2.5.8; B's phone offline state shows no offline text; C's palette lacks direct import/export commands; the measured phone canvas share for C was 64 % against its claimed 71 %.

synthesis.summary: Final design for the research annotation and overlay workspace (Stoipath Viewer, RUO) written to wsi-viewer/design/screens/final/research-annotation.html (273 KB, self-contained, links ../../design-system/tokens.css and base.css by relative path, no network). Base is the weighted winner B "Workbench" (Library left: Cohort/Slides/Layers; Context right: Inspector/Annotations/Model/Channels/Export; always-visible search field; rail with counted panel switchers; keyboard-resizable docks as grid tracks; laptop panel strip; widget = same node in a notebook cell). Grafted from C: "Slide 14 of 48 · 3 done" chip at every width, To do/In progress/Done filters and cohort progress, coverage bar, candidate-region queue with Fly there/reviewed marks, "Mark slide complete · next (N)", in-dock keymap/About/quality overlays (aria-modal=false, never over the slide), palette dropping over the Context column, in-flow peeking sheet below 1080 px with a 44 px labelled grab row and Library|Context switch, pointer-anchored wheel/is-gesturing/textContent-only HUD with reserved readout widths, explicit export targets + manifest + byte-identity jobs, full degraded-state inventory with §5 strings verbatim, whole-canvas deutan/protan simulation incl. swatches, Clinical-IH/Dx variants with the D1 "QA review · blinded" chip, accession, synthetic patient line, label image, NAV/DX, not-validated marker, launch-refused plate. Grafted from A: focus mode (\) as the canvas-maximal escape hatch with the HUD tool line and 24 px counted class legend, tool wheel at the pointer with class ring, inline typed zoom (no prompt()), quality sheet, per-device channel-cap reasons, first-run hint retired by commandInvoked. Demo controls kept (build, surface, slide, view, 13 states, panels, focus/legend, keymap/palette/wheel, mouse/pen, CVD, live markers, centre guide, hide review chrome, canvas-share readout) plus query parameters for screenshots. Collapsed "Design decisions" section lists provenance per element, the judges' disagreements and resolutions, fixes applied, design notes D-F1–D-F11 and the engine-contract map. Screenshots (DPR 1) at 3840x2160, 1920x1080, 1440x900, 1024x1366, 1366x1024, 390x844 plus 21 state variants in design/screens/final/shots/; all were viewed and problems fixed (nested-button boot error, Clinical-IH top-bar overflow, navigator intrusion with the laptop drawer, hidden layer rows removed by base.css .is-hidden, sub-24 px targets, curtain/side-by-side label collisions, channel-row truncation, palette double truncation, launch-refused panel content, widget placeholder). Measured canvas share of the product frame at rest: 76 % (4K), 72 % (1920), 85 % (1440), 85 % (1366 pen), 81 % (1024 portrait), 76 % (phone); 92 % in focus mode.
notes: Judges' disagreement resolved as documented in the page's Design decisions section: B's IA (weighted winner, engineering pick) carries C's safety scaffolding and accessibility (pathologist and UX picks) and A's collapsed-chrome mode; the step metaphor itself is not kept because the pathologist's own condition ('all-steps default') reduces C to a dock plus progress indicator.

In-flow sheet (C) chosen over overlay sheets (A/B) on tablets and phones; the engineering cost (canvas resize on expand) is carried as Design note D-F2 with a defer-while-gesturing mitigation, to be measured against NFR-P9 on W60.

Design notes for the plan/design-system owner (D-F1–D-F11 in the page): docks as grid tracks resize the canvas between gestures; model jobs, uncertainty queue, 'Mark slide complete' and collection state are research-package services, not engine contracts; base.css defects: navigator pan buttons 24 px hover-only, phone badge below 44 px, .segmented__item computes to 18 px, and .layer-row.is-hidden is killed by the .is-hidden utility (all three concepts carried it; this page uses .is-off); four proposed bindings (\ focus, ⇧G grid, ⇧V wheel, N mark complete); D1 purpose chip 'QA review · blinded' used instead of A's non-D1 string; channel pseudo-colours need the same ΔE00 warning; strip notice priority transient > error > Dx > multiplex > tiler.

Canvas share is reported two ways in the demo readout: of the product frame (P1 test) and of the viewport including the review header/demo strip; 1920×1080 is 72 % / 68 %, so the viewport figure dips below 70 % only because of review chrome; 'Hide review chrome' (or ?chrome=0) removes it.

By-design central-50 % exemptions remaining in the audit: the per-pane labels in the channel grid (a user-invoked canvas mode) and the tool wheel when opened from the keyboard/demo at the canvas centre (a transient, user-invoked GPU layer, exempt like the pen-tip palette). 6 px dock resizers are keyboard separators, as the judges accepted.

Query parameters for screenshots/review: product (ruo|clinical|dx), surface=widget, slide (he|ihc|if), view (single|side|curtain|grid), state (normal, cold4g, offline-pack, offline-nopack, tile-error, server-slow, soft-level, tier2, dx-refused, context-loss, manifest-fail, launch-refused, py-sync), lib/ctx (tab or 0), sheet=1, focus=1, legend=1, pen=1, cvd (deutan|protan), heat=1, grid=1, mag, fly, tool, keymap=1, about=1, quality=1, palette=1&q=, wheel=1, live=1, guides=1, theme=light, chrome=0, decisions=1, hint=0. The mock reads the URL but never writes it and never calls prompt() (anywidget/iframe hosts).

Screenshot tooling: Playwright (/opt/node-tools, browsers in /opt/pw-browsers), script at <scratch>/ra-final/shoot.js; touch viewports used hasTouch/isMobile so (pointer: coarse) rules applied; reducedMotion: 'reduce'. A DOM/runtime check (domcheck.js) found no duplicate ids, no nested or unlabelled buttons, no external resources and no errors while exercising keys, palette, overlays, products, slides, views and viewport changes.

Known mock limitations are stated in the page: SVG tissue patterns, 3,200 generated centroids for 1.24 M detections, pinch/pen pressure not simulated, jobs/queue/tiler shown as states; content is synthetic (CAMELYON16 identifiers are public CC0; patient line and label image are placeholders marked data-synthetic).
